focus: So Min-ho May 14-19 release-delay chain, prosecution framing, and judicial/prosecutorial actor expansion

material_findings.finding: NIHK's constitutional-history DB identifies the exact Korean primary target for the Assembly release action as National Assembly Secretariat, 12th regular session stenographic record No.57, 1952-05-14. FRUS document 135 independently states that the Assembly acted on May 14 under Constitution Article 49.

A contemporaneous Chosun Ilbo report preserved by NIHK fixes physical release on 1952-05-19, followed by So Min-ho leaving prison at about 20:00, visiting the National Assembly secretariat, and returning home. This confirms a real gap between the May 14 Assembly action and May 19 physical release.

The current evidence does not yet identify the legal/custodial cause of the five-day gap. Later historical accounts attribute the release to Busan District Court judge An Yun-chul's suspension-of-detention decision after prosecutors did not execute the Assembly demand, but the original court order and prosecution/corrections paperwork remain the required primary targets.

Prosecutor General Han Kyok-man publicly announced on 1952-05-10 that the shooting was a simple individual criminal act without political character. His published charging narrative names So's Interior/Security Committee specialist Jeong Jin-dong and escorts Seo Won-ryong, Kim Cheo-jung and Lee Jong-seok, creating additional institutional actor leads independent of the later political interpretation of the case.

The April 25 Seoul Shinmun account and May 10 prosecution announcement conflict on important incident details, including reported shooting time (21:30 versus 20:40) and arrest framing. These should remain source-specific observations until Report Nos.1-3, police records and trial evidence are opened.

The April 25 contemporary report explicitly explains the Article 49 issue: a member could be arrested in flagrante, while release during session could follow an Assembly demand. This is useful contemporaneous legal framing but must still be checked against the 1948 constitutional text and Record No.57 debate.

NIHK modern-person data identifies Han Kyok-man 韓格晩 and preserves conflicting birth-date/year variants. His identity can be promoted as a verified institutional actor while the lifespan conflict remains explicit.

A modern judicial-history source identifies An Yun-chul 安潤出 as the judge who ordered suspension of detention and reports subsequent threats; another biographical source gives 1911-1994 and a post-liberation judicial career. Because the original 1952 order has not been opened, his event role is candidate/strong-lead rather than primary-verified.

FRUS document 138 independently establishes that the first government act under martial law was So Min-ho's re-arrest early May 25, followed by arrests of opposition legislators. This remains separate from the unresolved authorship of the Korean re-arrest order.

The archival catalog for NARA Box 15 confirms three distinct Korean investigation-report objects (Report No.1 committee investigation, No.2 So Min-ho statement, No.3 prosecution investigation), plus trial summary, photographs and scene/weapon photographs. These are the highest-value originals for separating committee findings, defendant claims and prosecution claims.

adversarial_checks: Did not equate the May 14 Assembly resolution with physical release; the May 19 contemporary report proves a five-day execution gap.
Did not accept later claims that prosecutors refused release as primary fact; original prosecution/court/corrections records remain required.
Did not treat An Yun-chul's reported role as primary-verified without the original detention-suspension order.
Kept Han Kyok-man's statement that the case was nonpolitical as a contemporaneous prosecution position rather than objective resolution of political context.
Compared April 25 press and May 10 prosecution accounts and preserved conflicting shooting-time details instead of harmonizing them.
Did not infer that the May 25 martial-law declaration was solely for So Min-ho from the fact that his re-arrest was the first reported act.
Did not infer the author of the May 25 re-arrest order from FRUS's sequence description.
Did not merge the Assembly specialist Jeong Jin-dong with a NIHK politician/person entry of the same Hanja without personnel evidence.
Did not promote So Min-ho's escorts to politician nodes; they remain institutional-official/witness candidates pending evidence of political office.
Did not use later summaries to resolve guilt/self-defense; Report Nos.1-3 and trial evidence remain separate provenance objects.

history_debt_updates.update: The So Min-ho branch now separates May 14 Assembly release resolution, May 14-19 execution gap, May 19 physical release, and May 25 martial-law re-arrest. An Yun-chul is a strong candidate judicial actor for the May 19 release decision, but original court/prosecution/corrections records are still missing. Re-arrest order authorship and presidential command link remain unresolved.

floor_note: The requested 40-document, 20-line, 10-politician, 8-event and 8-existing-debt floors were not reached in this execution window. Counts are not padded. The main advance is separation of the May 14 legislative act from the May 19 physical release, plus creation of a testable judicial/prosecutorial chain rather than a single undifferentiated 'release' event.
